description: There is no way to refuse a pairing request in the UI. The page says 'If it does not, close this page; the request expires on its own.' although a deny route exists, so a security-minded user cannot actively reject a suspicious request and the request stays valid up to 10 minutes.
evidence: screenshots/step-1.png (no Deny); snapshot lists Approve only
suggested_fix: Add a Deny link next to the card title or under Approve that calls the existing deny route.

description: The Account row, which shows which signed-in account will own the drive, is only inside the collapsed Details; users with two accounts could approve under the wrong one.
expected: Show the account name outside Details or in the header.
suggested_fix: Show 'Signed in as <email>' under the title.

description: The card's question 'Does this code match your terminal?' puts the 8-letter code first, while the check that matters is the 16-hex verification code.
expected: Label the two codes by purpose ('Pairing code' vs 'Verification code').
suggested_fix: Rename to 'Pairing code (check it matches)' and explain the second field.

description: An incomplete code (12 hex digits without spaces) gets 'as four groups like a1b2 c3d4 e5f6 7890', implying spaces are required although `2B1A4C4B82B6953F` is accepted.
With Details expanded at 1280x800 the Approve button is below the fold.
suggested_fix: Make Details compact or keep the action row sticky.
